subject: Atlas AI — committed GPU sizing and short-term fleet plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Atlas AI — sizing baseline + recommmendations for committed capacity

Team —

Following up from last week's call with Atlas (DL-8743). They asked for a concrete committed plan for Dedicated to support their production workload in Q1. I pulled the usage CSV and Markus' profile summary, and sketched a short-term plan. Key asks:

- Confirm baseline steady-state GPUs to commit for 12 months (they want predictability).
- Propose a 30-day ramp / burst plan for their expected feature launch Jan 15.
- Call out fallback option: temporary burst from hosted pool vs. adding hardware tranche.

Attached: Atlas-Dedicated-Sizing-Workbook.xlsx (workbook with utilization tabs).

Initial recommendation (high level):
- Commit 48 A10G-equivalent GPUs as a baseline (estimated 95th pct utilization headroom at current patterns).
- Leave 12-GPU burst buffer (hosted/dedicated burst policy) for spikes during rollout.
- Re-evaluate after 8 weeks of production telemetry and right-size then.

Markus — can you confirm the utilization assumptions (p50/p95 tokens per second, KV cache hit) and whether 48 baseline is defensible? Laura — we need procurement cue — if they sign commit, what's typical lead / billing cadence? Monica — I'll need a short mutually agreed action plan (MAP) to send to Claire.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales (West) | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-02T10:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas AI — sizing baseline + recommmendations for committed capacity

Vanessa —

Quick validation from infra side after running the workbook through the perf model. I pulled Atlas' last 90 days: p50 token RPM ~= 42k, p95 ~= 210k; average KV cache hit ~ 78%. Those numbers map to roughly 0.9 req/s per model shard for A10G at median L2 seq lengths.

My notes:
- 48 baseline GPUs is reasonable for CURRENT traffic if they keep KV hit >= 75%; it gives ~15-20% headroom at p95.
- If their launch increases p95 by 1.5x, we'll need +24 GPUs (total 72) or enable aggressive batching and raise queue time tolerance.
- Burst buffer: prefer reserved burst (dedicated reserved but inactive nodes that can be spun up) rather than hosted pool for data residency reasons they mentioned. That means lead time for physical allocation is ~7-10 days.

Action items for MAP:
1) Ask Atlas to confirm expected peak multiplier for launch (1.2x vs 1.5x).
2) Agree on KV cache SLAs (target >=75%).
3) Finance sign-off on commit tiers (48 / 72 / 96). Laura — can you run ballpark OPEX impact for 48 vs 72 for 12-month term?

-Markus
Sr. Infra PM | Redwood Inference

Proposed commitment (12 months):
- Baseline committed capacity: 48 A10G-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool).
- Short-term launch buffer: 24 GPUs reserved for 30 days surrounding Jan 15 launch, with the option to convert to committed capacity if sustained.
- Fallback: On-call hosted pool burst up to 12 GPUs for emergency traffic above reserved buffer; billed at hosted rates.

2) Redwood to provide final cost/term sheet and DocuSign link by Nov 13.

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple clarifications from our side before we lock:

- Expected peak multiplier: based on staging load tests, we expect ~1.35x P95 for the first two weeks of launch, normalizing to ~1.1x after that as caching warms.
- KV cache: our caching layer is in active development — target is 80% but we expect 70-75% day 0. We can commit to configuration work with Redwood's solutions team to reach 78% within 30 days.
- Residency: we need guaranteed dedicated nodes for the baseline (no hosted fallback for baseline). Burst from hosted pool acceptable only for emergency > 95th pct.

Can you confirm price delta for converting reserved 24 GPUs to committed mid-term? Also want DocuSign routing to our procurement lead (procurement@atlas.ai).

Vanessa / team —

I ran the cost scenarios for 12-month committed terms. High-level: 
- 48 GPUs committed: list-equivalent OPEX reduction ~22% vs on-demand, monthly committed charge matches their forecast budget.
- 72 GPUs committed (if they convert reserved 24 to committed): incremental monthly add ~ +50% vs 48; unit price improves ~10% at that tier.
- Conversion: we offer a prorated conversion credit — if they convert the 24 reserved to committed within the 30-day reserve window, we waive the provisioning fee and apply a pro-rata credit back to start of the billing month.

Procurement note: need procurement@atlas.ai contact on DocuSign envelope, and PO issued within 10 business days post-signature. Monica — can you draft the MAP doc and include the DocuSign routing?
